reviews.comment: Fletcher is a great prof! Exams are open-note and online, but info comes from in-class lectures, so make sure to take good notes. There are no quizzes, only two exams, an individual podcast assignment, and an essay. His expectations are very clear, and it is very easy to get a good grade in the course. Take Fletcher if you can!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher and a great guy. lectures were very interesting. As long as you show up to lecture and take notes you will get an A on all exams. Exams are open note. No slides or anything on canvas so you do need to show up to class. spent no time on this class outside of class. would 100% take again.
Awesome professor, he made history so entertaining. His lectures are so funny and he gives little to no work. Exams are online and open note!
Reading and writing assignments due every class. Big group project at the end of the semester that includes public speaking.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor super funny.  He does not do slides so you have to be there if you want to take notes. 2 online exams but the info comes straight from his lectures or the textbook. One paper and podcast assignment. Overall very interesting class and fairly easy if you go to class and take the notes.
Very easy class, graded by 2 online exams, a podcast, and an essay. I spent a very minimal amount of time working on this class and ended w an easy A.

Great Professor! After taking him, I want another class with Dr. Fletcher! He is very lecture heavy since that's what will be on the tests so go to class, but he makes it super enjoyable! I was never bored in a lecture. Take Dr. Fletcher he's awesome! Also make sure you read his sources…it will help like crazy!
His tests come from his lectures so go to class. He has very enjoyable lectures too so that's a plus. Sit close to the front if you can. Dr. Fletchers a goat, talk to him about baseball

So glad I took this professor! He has such a sweet personality, and he makes lectures so much more fun and interesting than what I've heard other professors do. Assignments are very easy, and there are only 2 exams (midterm and final), which are also not stressful at all, and he makes the time to meet with students continuously too! Best prof! :D

Dr. Fletcher is great. I have taken 3 courses with him and he really is passionate about history. While this course did have a mock court group assignment that is because it is a part of the legal history certificate. Come to class, do the readings, interact and participate, and do the weekly assignments and you will be more than fine. Great prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor for HIST 105. 2 exams (online, open note) and 2 projects (essay, podcast). Exams are really easy if you attend lectures. He knows what he is talking about, is passionate, and he strives for class participation in lectures. Essay and podcast aren't bad and they're graded lightly. Highly recommend.

Dr Fletcher is nice guy but the Mock Court Project is completely irrelevant to the actual Class subject. It's clear that this class is for people interested in Legal history, which was not my expectation coming into this class. If you hate group projects DO NOT take, since it will compose most of the class structure and grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: A lot of papers and a lot of readings. The classes feel very unstructured in a way. If you are used to lecture heavy history classes then you will have a culture shock because this class is discussion based. Pretty chill guy though.

This class was lecture heavy, but most people stopped showing up because attendance wasn't mandatory (only one day was and the class was packed compared to what it was during the semester on that day). Only 2 exams on Canvas and 2 projects, a podcast and paper, textbook given online. This class wasn't difficult after all I would highly recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I cannot recommend Prof Fletcher enough for HIST 105/106. Attendance is not mandatory Mon&Wed but is Fri for a group podcast. Prof Fletcher thrives off of class engagement. It takes a while to get used to but it becomes enjoyable after. The few assignments due include a group project, 1 paper, 2 open note tests, and about 3 more.

Dr. Fletcher is amazing at lectures and he made the content very interesting. I enjoyed going to every lecture because of his personality and how presented the information. Exams are very easy if you take  notes during class. Group podcast episodes are graded fairly, but were time consuming and need a good group to divide the work.

It isn't very good. You do three podcast episodes in which you work with about 12 people in the group project. If you get an awful group, you're probably gonna get an awful grade on the podcast. His class is very awfully organized- his lectures, He always gets off-topic or just rambles, and you're trying to catch up. It's very hard to take notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor. The only reason I got a B is because I didn't submit a lab report for the podcast, which was the only thing that cut my points off.

not a hard class but the prof is extremely difficult to work with. the podcasts he has you do are so terrible especially if you get a bad group. I ended up doing all the work for 12 people because I had no choice if I wanted to save my own grade.
great professor that makes the content easy to digest, easy A.

Loved his lectures they were quite interesting. Overall very easy class with a flexible grading structure mainly based off of group podcasts. I had errors with my test where it kicked me out and he was very understanding and allowed me to retake it. 10/10 would take again.

The class was simple and make sure to get the notes from class as his entire test is based on his lectures. Podcast recordings aren't too bad just make sure you have outlines ready to go so your group can split the work up nicer. The paper is a little hard as it really depends on how the TA grades them so make sure to ask about your paper.

Dr. Fletcher's class is not too bad. His instructions for the paper were a bit unclear but everything else was pretty clear, and he is not a tough grader on podcasting labs as others have mentioned as long as you put a good effort into it. Lectures are not mandatory, but attending lectures makes the midterm and final open-note exams easy.

History 365 was structured as a discussion based course where you would read material, write a small essay on your thoughts regarding it, and then he would grade both that and your contributions to the class wide discussion. The Methodism project was very time consuming and required a lot of research but he graded it fairly and was very helpful
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This class wasnt awful, but was def not my fav. You have a semester long group podcast project, but its really not hard to get an A on each episode as long as you try. Lectures are so boring & he talks forever so i never went on mondays. There is 2 tests which arent bad but the paper was horrible. The guidelines & rubric for it were weird. id rec

The group project for this class was one of the worst group projects I've ever had, you weren't allowed to do it out of class, but it was more work than could easily be done in class. He doesn't get through all the material since he goes on tangents and tries to get you to guess the idea he's thinking of, yet tests you over material he didn't teach
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: literally the easiest class because the majority of your grade is just group podcasts. besides that, we do have one essay but it's pretty simple. attendance is mandatory on podcast days but you do wanna go on other days too because his exams are word for word what he says (online, not proctored). just write everything down and you'll be set

Dr. Fletcher was funny and engaging which made going to  5:45pm class not as bad. It is a lot of reading but all at tamu library so no purchases needed. Journal entries over readings every monday. 2 big papers and one small mapping research project. It hard the week they are due but better than quizzes and test. Discussion based class not lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, I had him in Fall 2023, and he was very lenient on grading our group podcasts. Other professors have their students do book reports on the textbook while Fletcher provides a free textbook and had us do simple group podcasts. The only time you work outside of class time is when studying for the midterm and final.

He is a bit quirky at times but gives a great lecture. You can tell he is passionate about history. He's super helpful in office hours and his syllabus is one of the most detailed I have ever seen. The group podcast assignment wasn't ideal but if you put in the organization and work you'll be fine.

To start, I SUCK at history. Dr. Fletcher made 105 a breeze. The class is podcast based. Each unit has 4-6 readings, and you get assigned a group of ~10 that you keep for the whole semester, Together, you split the readings and record a 12min podcast each week in class. The 2 tests are online and open note, so just Ctrl-F the answers. Easy A.

Dr. Fletcher is a very fun & caring professor. Tests are open note & open textbook, group projects are graded easily & lots of assistance is there if needed. Would take his class again & again. Lecture not necessary but very interesting if attended

Dr. Fletcher is very... passionate. He keeps you entertained during lectures. However, he gets excited about topics and has a habit of screaming into the mic. The whole class is based on group podcasts that you create. That being said, If you get stuck with a suckey group just drop.

Dr. Fletcher's class was fairly easy. I was worried about the podcast project at the beginning, but it wasn't bad at all. He was not always the friendliest, but his TA was very nice so I talked to her. Attendance isn't mandatory on Monday and Wednesday, but you will do poorly on exams if you do not go.

he's a good prof but the class is extremely unorganized.the majority of yr grade depends on the group u work with for the whole semester and make podcasts with. almost no time given in class and he gets mad if you work outside. takes forever to give feedback on podcasts and also the tests are lecture heavy. good class but needs to be restructured.

Lectures M/W with Friday being the podcast day. Go to lectures for notes on the exams!! The whole semester is a group project but once you figure out how to do the podcasts it is very easy. No homework, max 30 mins a week just drafting up your podcast script. 2 online/open note tests, and one group paper in which you only have to write a paragraph.

Seems like a nice guy, but this class is a joke. Supposed to get to reconstruction, but with only a few weeks left, just now finished the American Rev. Guy gets off on too many side stories - expects us to know things off top of our heads, then gets mad when we don't know it.  Aren't you supposed to be teaching us?  Weekly podcasts are a waste.

He was cool, a little bit ego-y but still had a great class. Anyone who says he's bad rlly just hates doing work tbh. I don't like a lot of work and I still enjoyed the class. Just split the readings with your given group and WRITE A SCRIPT BEFORE RECORDING

If you don't like history OR don't tend to test well, TAKE DR. FLETCHER!!! This year we had two exams, both take home and open note, and no other tests. All grades for the term are podcast episodes you record with your designated team. As someone who doesn't test well, this let me prepare all of my work beforehand and do well.

He provides you with the textbook for free. The only time attendance is mandatory is during the podcasting labs. He doesn't take many grades, and the bulk will come from your group. He teaches hidden history lessons, so it's refreshing to not have the same history lessons from 5th grade onward. Engaging and you won't struggle to hear him.

Honesty pretty easy class, amazing lecturer and drawer. Took him for 105 and 226 and its been fun going to class. Just go to lecture and take notes, especially when he draws it on the screen. Biggest part of grade is podcasts, which are group projects are most of your grade. Go to class and you will get an A.
Fletcher is awesome. His class is kind of weird, because almost all of your grade comes from recording podcasts with a group, but it's honestly really easy. Tests are hard if you skip class.

Dr. Fletcher really enjoys teaching! Your class grade mainly comes from group projects, but if your team tries, it can be really fun! He does try a little too "extra" to relate to students and to get them to laugh, but his lectures are very engaging and can have lots of entertaining discussions and student commentary!

I would not take this class as a hybrid if Aggie Schedule builder shows only one day a week. There's so much group project work needed to be done outside of class, and a ton of busy work that would leave you feeling stressed during exam week. You have to do an online notebook, podcasts, and multiple labs and it's a lot. But there are no exams.

THIS CLASS SUCKS 
way to much busy work and all around pointless also making all of the podcast sucks
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: his lectures are so entertaining and easy to follow along to
favorite professor, group projects were fun and he gave us time in class to do them.

I enjoyed Professor Fletcher because he was easy to understand and follow. He was heavy on lectures, so the bulk of things you would need to know are by attending class everyday. I recommend writing everything down because the majority of things he says is on the exams verbatim. The group project is easy, just show up every Friday and do your part.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The textbook required for his class is provided by Mr. Fletcher.

If you're thinking about taking him, do it. His lectures are fun (as fun as history can be), and he's just a super chill dude in general. Most of the class is graded on a big group project you work on over the whole semester, but it's really easy. Tests are open-note and weighted really low. 10/10 :)
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr Fletcher is a great professor who loves history. As someone with little interest in history he made lectures entertaining enough to pay attention. Most of grade is a group project which goes throughout the whole semester and is graded lightly if you put in effort. I enjoyed having him as a professor and would definitely choose him again.

Dr. Fletcher is a very animated lecturer but I still managed to find myself not paying attention. It's okay though since most of the exams are based on class readings. All of the exams are also online. He LOVES group projects that continue throughout the semester.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fletcher is very funny, his lectures are engaging, and you can tell he really cares about the class. He welcomes comments and questions during his lectures. His tests are open note and super easy. Much of the grade is participation in group projects.

Fletcher was great! He made this class enjoyable and easy! As long as you get the notes, you'll be good. There were only two tests, a midterm and a final and they were open note and online and were easy. The majority of the grade was the group projects he made us do, but was not hard at all. Take him if you can!

Dr. Fletcher is a national treasure. His lectures are incredibly engaging and interesting. I was genuinely sad when his classes got cancelled. He's incredibly funny, and the chemistry he developed with the rest of the class made it so that every class was entertaining. If the other reviews haven't convinced you yet, you would be wise to take him.

One of the best professors I've ever had. I never thought I would say this, but he actually makes history fun to learn about through the way he teaches us. He is so funny! He makes the whole class laugh every single lecture. I'm taking 226 with him next semester. This is the first time I've taken the same prof twice.

Dr. Fletcher is an incredible professor, and this is definitely one of the best history classes I've taken! Tests were open note and online and group assignments and lectures are fun and engaging! I definitely recommend taking 105 with Dr. Fletcher!
Definitely one of my favorite classes so far. Very friendly and he'll be willing to help any student.
He is an incredibly easy going professor who is funny. All tests were open note and online. The course schedule is very clear and well organized. I highly recommend!

Really funny guy. Took him for 105, not 226. Group podcasts weekly- sure, but if you have a communicative group it's simple enough. Lectures are engaging and he constantly encourages the class to add in, leading to tons of funny moments. I probably let out a legitimate laugh at least twice every lecture(tho maybe my class is just special). A++ Prof
BEST TEACHER EVER! Easy A in my opinion.

I actually took him for HIST105 but that wasn't a course option for him. He is an amazing prof and really engages the entire class the he's lecturing, even the kids in the very back row were involved and actively listening to what he had to say. I loved this guy and im taking his 226 class next semester. Highly recommend.

reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy and clear lectures, makes it easy to learn material for exams!

Professor Fletcher's approach to lecturing is, in my opinion, highly inappropriate and it shows his clear lack of experience and organization. It took him 6 classes (three weeks) for him to even begin lecturing, and when he did, it wasn't even relevant to Texas history. His lectures have no substance and he's wasting our time and money.
